commits_this_run: 09cc4ad fix(ops): bound a delegated operator grant by the issuer's own deadline (NEX-084)
decisions_this_run: The ceiling is the FURTHEST covering grant, not the nearest. An issuer who holds a scope for a week has not narrowed their authority by also holding an unrelated five-minute grant of the same scope; refusing on the nearer one would reject a hand-out their authority plainly covers.

A settings-seeded operator has an unbounded grant (expires_at=None), so their ceiling is None and existing deployments are unaffected. Reading the ceiling from the store rather than from configuration keeps one source of truth for what the gate believes.

409 Conflict, not 403. The caller is authorized to issue grants; the requested grant conflicts with the issuer's own authority. A 403 would assert the caller may not issue at all, which is false, and would collide with the ADR-008 permission split.
Scope and lifetime are read in a single store call at the gate's clock, so attenuation cannot pass against a grant that has lapsed by the time the lifetime is compared.

A state file can be stale in the reassuring direction (run 83 recorded two slices of delivery debt that did not exist). GitHub prose is read from the API and section counts asserted before any append.
run_summary: Run 84 delivered NEX-084: operator-grant delegation attenuated scope but not lifetime, so a holder of a one-hour incident grant could issue the same scope for thirty days and hand on authority they never had. IssueOperatorGrant now reads the issuer's live grants once, at the gate's clock, and refuses with 409 when the requested expiry outlives the furthest instant they hold that scope until; a wildcard covers scope and horizon, and an unbounded own grant leaves the ceiling unbounded so settings-seeded operators are unaffected.
